::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **Time:** 35 minutes
- **You produce:** one merged pull request that adds the section "Research question and scope" to the README and closes the Issue E01-T2.
- **New terms:** [branch](../cheat-sheet.qmd#branch), [commit](../cheat-sheet.qmd#commit), [pull request](../cheat-sheet.qmd#pull-request), [review](../cheat-sheet.qmd#review), [merge](../cheat-sheet.qmd#merge). All terms are in the [cheat sheet](../cheat-sheet.qmd).
:::

## Why this step

In X1 you changed `main` directly. That is acceptable for a first README, but it skips two safeguards. A **branch** keeps a change apart until it is ready. A **pull request** shows the change, links it to the Issue that asked for it, and invites a **review** before the change enters `main`.

The link between the pull request and the Issue closes the loop of the plan. The keyword `Closes #4` in the pull request description tells GitHub to close Issue #4 when the pull request merges. The Project workflows then move the item to **In review** when the link appears and to **Done** when the Issue closes. The plan and the work agree without extra clicks.

A review is a human check against the acceptance criteria. An automatic AI reviewer can appear if your account enables it. In the test run on 12 October 2026, it failed with a quota message. Do not treat an AI review as the review.

## Before you start

- You finished [X3](x3.qmd). Issue E01-T2 exists. Note its number (for example `#4`).
- Command-line route: open a terminal in the folder `projm-thesis`. Define the helper `issue` as in [X3](x3.qmd#before-you-start), if this is a new terminal:

  ```bash
  issue() { gh issue list --state all --limit 100 --json number,title \
    --jq ".[] | select(.title | startswith(\"$1 \")) | .number"; }
  ```
- Pair up if possible. Your partner reviews your pull request, and you review theirs.

## Steps

### Edit on a new branch

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open `README.md` and click the pencil icon.
2. Place the cursor before the line `## Visibility`.
3. Paste the text below.
4. Click **Commit changes…**.
5. Type the message `docs: add research question and scope`.
6. Select **Create a new branch for this commit and start a pull request**. Keep the proposed branch name or type `docs/e01-t2-scope`.
7. Click **Propose changes**.

#### Command line

1. Create a branch for E01-T2 and switch to it. The branch is linked to the Issue.

   ```bash
   gh issue develop $(issue E01-T2) --name docs/e01-t2-scope --checkout
   ```

2. Open `README.md` in a text editor.
3. Paste the text below before the line `## Visibility`.
4. Save the file.
5. Save the change as a commit and send the branch to GitHub:

   ```bash
   git add README.md
   git commit -m "docs: add research question and scope"
   git push
   ```

:::

The text to paste:

```markdown
## Research question and scope

**Research question:** How did the landscape of Swiss periodicals change between 1830 and 1960 by language, place, and subject?

| In scope                                                  | Out of scope                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 30 synthetic periodical records (German, French, Italian) | Real archival records or digitised page images |
| Place, language, frequency, and years of publication      | Content analysis of articles                   |
| Reuse status of the fictional scans                       | Readers, subscribers, or other personal data   |

```

### Open the pull request

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Type the title `docs: add research question and scope`.
2. In the description, write `Closes #4` on the first line. Use the number of your E01-T2.
3. Copy the acceptance criteria of E01-T2 below it and tick the boxes that your change meets.
4. Click **Create pull request**.
5. Open your Project. E01-T2 now shows the Status **In review**. The Project workflow **Pull request linked to issue** sets it. The workflow runs with a delay. If the Status did not change, wait one minute and reload the page. If it still did not change, check the workflow as in [X3](x3.qmd).

{{< screenshot x4-pull-request >}}

{{< screenshot x3-workflow-in-review >}}

#### Command line

1. Print the number of your E01-T2 with `issue E01-T2`.
2. In a text editor, write the description of the pull request. Write `Closes #` and this number on the first line, for example `Closes #4`.
3. Copy the acceptance criteria of E01-T2 below it. Tick the boxes that your change meets: `- [x]`.
4. Save the description as `pr-body.md` in the folder that contains `projm-thesis`.
5. Open the pull request:

   ```bash
   gh pr create --title "docs: add research question and scope" --body-file ../pr-body.md
   ```

6. Check the Status of E01-T2 in the Project. The result is `In review`. The Project workflow **Pull request linked to issue** sets it.

   ```bash
   gh issue view $(issue E01-T2) --json projectItems --jq '.projectItems[] | .title + ": " + .status.name'
   ```

7. The workflow runs with a delay. If the result is not `In review`, wait one minute and run the command again.

:::

### Review and merge

::: {.panel-tabset group="route"}

#### Browser

1. Open the tab **Files changed**.
2. Check the change against each acceptance criterion.
3. Click **Submit review**. A partner selects **Approve**; on your own pull request, select **Comment** and write what you checked.
4. Return to **Conversation** and click **Merge pull request**, then **Confirm merge**.
5. Click **Delete branch**.
6. Open your Project. E01-T2 shows the Status **Done**. The workflow runs with a delay. If the Status did not change, wait one minute and reload the page.

{{< screenshot x4-files-changed >}}

#### Command line

1. Show the change and check it against each acceptance criterion:

   ```bash
   gh pr diff
   ```

2. Submit the review. On your own pull request, write a comment that says what you checked. A partner approves with `gh pr review NUMBER --approve`.

   ```bash
   gh pr review --comment --body "Checked the three acceptance criteria."
   ```

3. Merge the pull request and delete the branch. gh then switches your folder back to `main` and gets the merged state.

   ```bash
   gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
   ```

4. Check that E01-T2 is closed and that the Project shows `Done`:

   ```bash
   gh issue view $(issue E01-T2) --json state,projectItems --jq '.state, (.projectItems[] | .status.name)'
   ```

5. The workflow runs with a delay. If the result is not `CLOSED` and `Done`, wait one minute and run the command again.

:::

## Expected state

{{< screenshot x4-issue-closed >}}

- [ ] The pull request is merged.
- [ ] Issue E01-T2 is closed "as completed" by the pull request.
- [ ] The Project shows E01-T2 as **Done**.
- [ ] Milestone M1 shows progress.
- [ ] The README on `main` contains the new section.

## If something goes wrong

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Issue did not close. | The keyword is missing or has the wrong number. | Edit the pull request description before the merge. After the merge, close the Issue by hand and link the pull request. |
| You cannot approve your own pull request. | GitHub does not allow it. | Use **Comment**, or ask a partner. |
| The Status did not change. | The Project workflow is off or broken. | Open **Workflows**; check **Pull request linked to issue** and **Item closed**. Set the Status by hand. |
| "This branch has conflicts". | Someone else changed the same lines. | Click **Resolve conflicts**, keep both texts, and mark the conflict as resolved. |
| You committed to `main` instead. | Wrong option in the dialog, or no `git switch` before the commit. | Close the Issue by hand with a comment that links the commit. Use a branch next time. |
| A command fails. | Usually the installation, the sign-in, or the folder. | See [Command-line problems](../setup.qmd#command-line-problems), or do the step in the browser. |

## Alternatives

- **Pair:** exchange review rights. Add your partner as a collaborator so that they can approve.
- **Private path:** identical. Branch protection for private repositories needs a paid plan, but this exercise does not need it.
